summary: The bill bars admission to the US of any national or recent resident of designated countries with unreliable identity or background verification, including Iran, Somalia, North Korea, Afghanistan, and others added by the Secretary of State, with narrow exceptions for permanent residents, refugees, military members, diplomats, and case-by-case national interest waivers.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgetary matters. It focuses exclusively on immigration restrictions and does not authorize or affect any expenditures.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection. It is unrelated to taxation.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, public programs, or market regulations. The bill is silent on this topic.
The legislation does not mention firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues in any way.

This bill directly and primarily amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to prohibit admission of aliens from designated countries with inadequate identity verification capabilities. It expands existing restrictions from Presidential Proclamation 9645, adds new countries (e.g., Afghanistan, Sudan), creates enhanced vetting, and imposes penalties for violations. This is a clear effort to restrict immigration and strengthen border/security screening, aligning strongly with the +1 end of the spectrum.
The bill has no connection to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related healthcare regulations.
While the bill references national security and the Director of National Intelligence, it does not alter military budgets, defense spending levels, or armed forces policy.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are present.
The bill does not address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No references to schools, education funding, or school choice appear in the text.
The legislation is unrelated to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

While it includes removal proceedings and reentry bars for immigration violators, these are standard immigration enforcement mechanisms rather than broader criminal justice reforms or sentencing changes.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures are involved.
The bill has no fiscal or deficit implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not modify or reference foreign aid programs.
Unrelated to voting rights, election procedures, or voter ID requirements.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance provisions are included.
The bill contains nothing related to workers' rights, unions, or employment policy.
The bill is facially neutral on religion and does not create or modify religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
